newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Holyman to buy Union Shipping units.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Holyman to buy Union Shipping units.

text.p: Australian shipping group Holyman Ltd said it agreed in principle with Brierley Investments Ltd to buy the Australian shipping businesses of Union Shipping Group for A$58.3 million.
Holyman also said it expected to earn between A$14 million and A$16 million after tax in calendar 1996.

Holyman said the businesses to be acquired are Coastal Expressline, the second largest of four freight carriers across Bass Strait, Union Stevedoring Services, which serves the vessels of Coastal ExpressLine and other carriers, and Union Bulkships.

Union Bulkships provides port agency and freight sales services and operates the vessel Sina which provides a coastal liner service under contract with the Western Australian state government, it said.
The businesses are forecast to contribute earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of A$15.8 million in 1997, it said.

The EBIT is forecast to translate, subject mainly to the nature of funding of the acquisition, into a post-acquisition Holyman Group forecast after-tax profit for calendar 1997 in the range of A$19.7 million to A$21.7 million, the company said.
A company spokesman said the A$14-A$16 million forecast did not take the Union Shipping acquisition into account.
The acquisition is conditional on regulatory and other approvals and the raising of necessary funds, Holyman said.
Holyman said it expected to execute an agreement with Brierley Investments before the end of this week.

Turning to its first profit forecast, Holyman said the main matters considered were the recognition of a prospective loss from the new Holyman Sally Ferries service in its first year of operations and a review of the investment in Cat-Link.

The proportion of group pre-tax profit attributed to the ferry sector is expected to fall to about 30 percent to 35 percent, as a result of the start up year losses in Holyman Sally Ferries and the review of the Cat-Link investment.
This will to some extent be offset by an improvement in the dividend expected from Condor Ferries, it said.
Holyman's 66-2/3 percent owned Holyman Sally Ferries operates high speed and conventional ferry services in the English Channel.

Holyman will earn profits on the charter to Holyman Sally Ferries of three fast ferries and forecasts that in 1997 these profits will exceed the expected loss on the operations of Holyman Sally Ferries.

It said all ferry operators have been hit by continuing heavy price discounting of the ferry and tunnel operators on the high density Dover-Calais route but believes the level of discounting will not be sustained beyond this year.

"The directors remain confident that Holyman Sally Ferries is a sound business, and that in 1998 the operations of Holyman Sally Ferries will make a significant contribution to group results," it said.

Cat-Link A/S, Holyman's half owned Danish associate, will be hit by a lower than expected Danish government toll on the new Great Store Belt Bridge, which has opened for rail traffic and will open for road traffic in the summer of 1998.
Cat-Link is currently performing under budget but its results will benefit from the higher earning period during the northern summer months, it said.
Strategies to counter the lower toll and other competitive influences of the new bridge are being developed by Cat-Link, Holyman said.

Turning to 1998 earnings, Holyman said: "With an improvement in earnings from the ferry sector expected in 1998 together with the significant contribution from the newly acquired businesses, the directors are confident that shareholders can look forward to earnings growth for the company in 1998."
Holyman earned a net profit of A$21.86 million in 1996.
